category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your wedding was scheduled the same day as the Georgia-Florida game. Explain to your fiancée why the venue has TVs now.
response:
This is a delicate situation that requires transparency and, ideally, a touch of humor. Here’s one way to handle it:

---

"Sweetheart, I need to come clean about something before you walk down the aisle. You know how we picked this date because the leaves were turning and the venue was available? I *may* have been so blinded by love that I forgot an annual, high-stakes, borderline-holy obligation that falls on this exact Saturday. It’s the Georgia-Florida game.

So, about the TVs... I know we talked about a rustic, screen-free ceremony where our love is the only show. But a wedding is about merging two lives, and part of my life—a deeply ingrained, slightly irrational part—is devoted to this game. I realized I couldn't fully be present in the moment if a small, anxious part of my soul was wondering about third-down conversions.

Think of the TVs not as a distraction, but as a wedding favor for my side of the family, a way to turn what could be a source of fidgety anxiety into a communal, joyous background hum. Our first kiss as husband and wife will still be the highlight. It'll just be timed, preferably, during a TV timeout.

I promise you center stage. The TVs are just the set dressing for the reception. The real main event is us—and maybe Georgia's defense."

---

The key is to balance the absurdity of the devotion with absolute sincerity about the wedding itself. If you frame it as a quirk of your character that she's accepting along with all the wonderful things, it makes it a shared joke rather than just a selfish demand. Good luck—both with the conversation and the game.
